date_basis: UTC recording date. Some later observations were collected after midnight on 2026-10-14 in Asia/Shanghai while their recorded_at timestamps were still on 2026-10-13 UTC. The artifact filename retains the UTC date.
verification_scope: Actual native iOS Simulator observations against an isolated HTTP fixture. These results do not establish real Rust backend, NyxAgent or external provider integration.

environment.backend: Isolated local HTTP fixture with disposable authentication and durable simulated conversation state

request_count_basis: Each record contains cumulative fixture route counts since the latest clear-log or reset at collection time. Windows may overlap across records; counts must not be summed or treated as per-case increments. Dynamic conversation, session, agent, memory, key, provider, acknowledgement, approval, grant and login-code identifiers are replaced by route placeholders.
evidence_handling: Only reviewed observations, outcomes, timestamps, platform and normalized request counts are exported from the private journal. Raw response bodies, message text, credentials, account identifiers and private filesystem paths are omitted from this JSON. Separately reviewed screenshots contain only disposable fixture content and are referenced by repository-relative paths. Before-fix failures remain alongside the successful reruns.

Editing the stored title through native Chat settings sent one PATCH request and refreshed the history. The heading reflected the changed title.

Before the gesture repair, double-tapping Send in an existing conversation sent one turn request and one unintended Stop request. The native UI showed stopping followed by a cancelled persisted turn. Cancelled work did not offer Retry.

After the gesture and stream-cleanup repairs, double-tapping Send in an existing conversation sent one turn request and no Stop request. The reply was saved once, the composer cleared, model changes remained disabled for the saved conversation, and no stream-close error overlay appeared. Partial text during execution was recorded separately.
The native UI showed an assistant working state, multiple visible partial reply fragments and an enabled Stop control while the fixture turn was still running, before completion.

Tapping Stop after a visible partial reply showed stopping followed by the persisted partial reply and a stopped notice. Cancelled work did not offer Retry, and no stream-close error appeared. One explicit Stop request followed one admitted turn request.
An invalid avatar URL showed an inline validation error while preserving the entered display name. No profile update was submitted.
Saving the profile showed success feedback and disabled the submit control. Returning to Settings and reopening account security retained the saved display name and cleared avatar.
Cancelling the confirmation preserved the other session. Confirming sign-out removed the prepared browser session and showed success feedback while retaining the current signed-in account.

Copying the MFA setup key showed feedback. Backgrounding and foregrounding the app removed the setup-key copy and open actions while retaining a blank verification step. An incorrect confirmation code showed an inline error without signing out the account.

A valid confirmation enabled MFA with recovery codes initially hidden. Reveal, copy feedback and hide worked. The native share sheet opened and was dismissed without choosing a destination. On return, no export-success message appeared and the controls remained enabled.
After backgrounding and foregrounding the app, the one-time recovery-code section and its reveal, copy and share controls were absent. Enabled MFA state and the disable action remained.

An incorrect password when disabling MFA kept the account signed in with MFA enabled and displayed an inline error. A valid password followed by the native confirmation disabled MFA and restored the authenticator setup action.
Confirming sign-out for the current device returned to an empty sign-in form. Workspace content and the account back button were absent.

An incorrect password showed an inline error. Double-tapping a valid Sign In admitted one MFA challenge request. An incorrect factor retained the challenge, showed an inline error and cleared the factor input. A valid factor opened the Assistant workspace.

Signing out from Settings cleared the sign-in form. Logging in as a second disposable account showed only that account's profile and an empty conversation history, without the first account's saved conversation. A delayed profile read completed before the second login; this establishes ordinary account cache separation and does not exercise a late-response race.

Before the polling repair, the selected Agent detail still displayed running more than six seconds after the fixture status changed to idle. List polling continued, but only one detail read was sent. The screenshot showed the stale running state.

Before the draft repair, both the profile purpose and account-read permission had unsaved changes. Saving the profile succeeded but reset the unrelated permission toggle and disabled Save permissions. This transient discarded-draft state was observed through native accessibility; no screenshot was captured for it.

After the polling repair, the selected Agent automatically changed from running to idle within the five-second polling window. Its recent thread also stopped showing Running while the unsaved display-name draft remained intact. The selected detail was read again before returning to the list.

Saving the profile retained the unsaved Read account information switch and kept Save permissions actionable. Saving permissions retained the unsaved display name and kept Save profile actionable. Both directions were observed, with one profile PATCH and one grants PUT. The two representative screenshots show the retained switch and retained display-name draft respectively.

After an external profile change, saving the local display-name draft showed a conflict and retained the local draft without a PATCH request. Explicitly reloading and discarding adopted the externally changed name.

An unsaved guest-access change combined with an external service-grant change showed a permissions conflict without a grants PUT request. Explicitly discarding and reloading adopted the externally added platform service.

The All granted guest selection survived an injected HTTP 503 response. Retrying showed Permissions saved and retained the same selection. Two grants PUT requests included service, account-read and guest-access fields while omitting machine and saved-login fields; the existing platform-service guest level remained Use.
Empty required fields disabled creation. Entering a disposable handle and purpose enabled creation, and one POST opened the new specialist detail with success feedback and zero memories.

The platform-managed detail showed its ownership notice without toggle, credential or removal controls. The organization-member detail showed its read-only notice and controls. Optional metadata parsed successfully, and no mutation request was observed.

Entering a disposable replacement enabled Save credential. Going to the actual iOS Home screen and returning to Expo cleared the credential field and disabled Save credential. No credential PUT was sent; foreground reads were GET requests.

A fresh initial removal returned HTTP 409. Choosing the separate Remove only this service action then sent a follow-up DELETE with grant_scope=token and returned HTTP 200. The list showed successful removal and no removed row while retaining the other connections and the OAuth Pending state.

Missing-credential validation prevented creation without a POST. Backgrounding cleared an entered disposable credential while retaining the display name. Re-entering the credential and submitting sent one POST and opened the active service detail with success feedback and an empty replacement field.

The connection-specific key identifier was used. No real provider OAuth flow was exercised.

Only the permanent-deletion confirmation and Cancel preservation were observed. No DELETE request or successful purge was performed, so destructive completion remains unverified.
